Why we need to keep out the marketing and "new left" if we want to be successful. Fuck Reddit.
And millennials were supposed to be the most tech savvy and most marketing adverse generation ever because they grew up immersed in both. Instead we ended up with a generation of followers.

Hmm. It seems to me that there are plenty of millennials who are both tech savvy and marketing averse, though it isn't the general trend. Who could expect a whole generation of people to trend against everything they've been indoctrinated in, constantly, from every angle for as long as they've lived? It seems like an obvious consequence of their environment that the majority of millennials are heavily indoctrinated good capitalist citizens.

But the minority who aren't, for whom indoctrination has somewhat failed, is substantial....and we have to grow it. It can be done. Dissent has been cultivated before, and is being cultivated now.

So fuck Reddit. Resist the creep of influence from advertisers and marketers. Try to make a space where genuine communication can occur.

Years back there were stories about how they were going to be able to see through all the marketing and propaganda because of the environment they were being brought up in. In retrospect the "visionaries" writing the stories couldn't be more wrong. The millennials ended up as susceptible to marketing as any others.

The problem is marketing and propaganda are insidious. Most people don't recognize when they are being swayed. To be constantly skeptical and to get angry when propagandized are the best shields imo but to many that may seem like a miserable existence.

Oh yeah, I agree with that point entirely; I remember those stories and how naive they seemed even back then. In hindsight, it looks like fairly transparent propaganda. But it's important to me to acknowledge that a substantial, potentially quite powerful minority exist even within that generation. There are tons of dissident millennials, and it is possible that they will bring about sweeping social change.

Anger has its place, but a habitually angry existence doesn't seem to accomplish anything positive in my experience. It's very difficult and often unpleasant to remain aware of oppression, especially now when it is so horrific and ubiquitous. For me it is an ongoing process to cope with frustration and hopelessness that inevitably creep in when you're awake in a totalitarian society, while still striving to do something good while I can.
